arxiv-1807-09619.title: Multiple sclerosis lesion enhancement and white matter region estimation using hyperintensities in FLAIR images
arxiv-1807-09619.creator: Paulo G. de Lima Freire, Ricardo J. Ferrari
arxiv-1807-09619.description: A 2018 arXiv research paper by Paulo G. de Lima Freire, Ricardo J. Ferrari. Multiple sclerosis (MS) is a demyelinating disease that affects more than 2 million people worldwide. The most used imaging technique to help in its diagnosis and follow-up is magnetic resonance imaging (MRI). Fluid Attenuated Inversion Recovery (FLAIR) images are usually acquired in the context of MS because lesions often appear hyperintense in this particular image weight, making it easier for physicians to identify them.

arxiv-1809-02432.title: Additive multivariate Gaussian processes for joint species distribution modeling with heterogeneous data Accepted for publication in Bayesian Analysis
arxiv-1809-02432.creator: Jarno Vanhatalo, Marcelo Hartmann, Lari Veneranta
arxiv-1809-02432.description: Abstract Species distribution models (SDM) are a key tool in ecology, conservation and management of natural resources. Two key components of the state-of-the-art SDMs are the description for species distribution response along environmental covariates and the spatial random effect that captures deviations from the distribution patterns explained by environmental covariates.

arxiv-2106-02097.title: A Consciousness-Inspired Planning Agent for Model-Based Reinforcement Learning
arxiv-2106-02097.creator: Mingde Zhao, Zhen Liu, Sitao Luan, Shuyuan Zhang, Doina Precup, Yoshua Bengio
arxiv-2106-02097.description: Abstract We present an end-to-end, model-based deep reinforcement learning agent which dynamically attends to relevant parts of its state during planning. The agent uses a bottleneck mechanism over a set-based representation to force the number of entities to which the agent attends at each planning step to be small.

arxiv-2205-14142.title: Only Classical Parameterised States have Optimal Measurements under Least Squares Loss
arxiv-2205-14142.creator: Wilfred Salmon, Sergii Strelchuk, David R. M. Arvidsson-Shukur
arxiv-2205-14142.description: Abstract Measurements of quantum states form a key component in quantum-information processing. It is therefore an important task to compare measurements and furthermore decide if a measurement strategy is optimal. Entropic quantities, such as the quantum Fisher information, capture asymptotic optimality but not optimality with finite resources.

arxiv-2303-12231.title: Ultrafast artificial intelligence: Machine learning with atomic-scale quantum systems
arxiv-2303-12231.creator: Thomas Pfeifer, Matthias Wollenhaupt, Manfred Lein
arxiv-2303-12231.description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by Thomas Pfeifer, Matthias Wollenhaupt, Manfred Lein. We train a model atom to recognize hand-written digits in the range 0-9, employing intense light–matter interaction as a computational resource. For training, the images of the digits are converted into shaped laser pulses (data input pulses). Simultaneously with an input pulse, another shaped pulse (program pulse), polarized in the orthogonal direction, is applied to the atom and the system evolves quantum mechanically according to the time-dependent Schrödinger equation.

arxiv-2405-15002.title: Private Regression via Data-Dependent Sufficient Statistic Perturbation
arxiv-2405-15002.creator: Cecilia Ferrando, Daniel Sheldon
arxiv-2405-15002.description: Abstract Sufficient statistic perturbation (SSP) is a widely used method for differentially private linear regression. SSP adopts a data-independent approach where privacy noise from a simple distribution is added to sufficient statistics. However, sufficient statistics can often be expressed as linear queries and better approximated by data-dependent mechanisms.

arxiv-2406-10183.title: A SART-Based Iterative Inversion Methodology to Infer the Solar Rotation Rate from Global Helioseismic Data
arxiv-2406-10183.creator: S. G.Sylvain G. \lnm Korzennik, A.Antonio \lnm Eff-Darwich
arxiv-2406-10183.description: Abstract We present a new iterative rotation inversion technique based on the Simultaneous Algebraic Reconstruction Technique developed for image reconstruction. We describe in detail our algorithmic implementation and compare it to the classical inversion techniques like the Regularized Least Squares (RLS) and the Optimally Localized Averages (OLA) methods.

arxiv-2411-03774.creator: Shozen Dan, Joshua Tegegne, Yu Chen, Zhi Ling, Veronika K Jaeger, André Karch, Swapnil Mishra, Oliver Ratmann, on behalf of the Machine Learning & Global Health network
arxiv-2411-03774.description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by Shozen Dan, Joshua Tegegne, Yu Chen, Zhi Ling, Veronika K Jaeger, André Karch, Swapnil Mishra, Oliver Ratmann, on behalf of the Machine Learning & Global Health network. Social contact surveys are an important tool to assess infection risks within populations, and the effect of non-pharmaceutical interventions on social behaviour during disease outbreaks, epidemics, and pandemics.

arxiv-2505-21879.creator: Weiting Liu, Jiaxu Cui, Jiao Hu, En Wang, Bo Yang
arxiv-2505-21879.description: Abstract In science, we are interested not only in forecasting but also in understanding how predictions are made, specifically what the interpretable underlying model looks like. pmc-11431048.title: Anatomical Study of the Superficial Musculoaponeurotic System in Relation to the Zygomaticus Major
pmc-11431048.creator: Hyun-Jin Park, Mi-Sun Hur
pmc-11431048.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). Background: The superficial musculoaponeurotic system (SMAS) is crucial for the structural integrity and dynamics of facial expressions and is a particularly important consideration during facelift surgeries. This study investigated the anatomical structure and continuity of the SMAS at the site where the zygomaticus major (Zmj) originates, which is where the SMAS extends from the lateral to the anterior aspects of the face. Knowledge of these aspects is crucial for understanding the mechanics of facial movements and also the aging process.

pmc-11523941.title: An apparent quandary: adoption of polygenics and gene panels for personalised breast cancer risk stratification
pmc-11523941.creator: Jerry S Lanchbury, Holly J Pederson
pmc-11523941.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2023). Over the past 30 years, genetic and epidemiological advances have revolutionised the prediction of breast cancer risk in women with significant family history. By screening these women for high- and intermediate-risk pathogenic variants and by interrogating their genomes for multiple lower-risk single-nucleotide polymorphisms (SNPs), we can provide individually tailored risk profiles in carriers of Mendelian breast cancer risk variants and in non-carriers, but clinical implementation of this approach is suboptimal.

pmc-11551430.description: SignificanceIn this study, we aimed to better understand the significance of the ability of Shigella to survive plasma exposure, as we observed that nonpathogenic Escherichia coli rapidly lysed upon exposure. Indeed, we reported that Shigella was exposed to plasma components first within the colonic mucosa, upon local hemorrhages, and then during bacteremia.

pmc-12457159.title: Hepatic involvement as an initial manifestation of multiple myeloma: a case report with atypical imaging features
pmc-12457159.creator: Zongsheng Pu, Lujiang Zhan, Yimi Zha, Yilin Li, Shilin Qiu, Yinfu He, Yanhong Yang, Zaihui Feng, Xingxing Zhu
pmc-12457159.description: Hepatic involvement as the initial manifestation of multiple myeloma (MM) is exceedingly rare and presents significant diagnostic challenges due to its heterogeneous imaging features, which often mimic metastatic liver tumors. We report a case of a 62-year-old man presenting with right upper quadrant discomfort.

pmc-12512955.title: Adaptation of the basic resuscitation skills self-efficacy scale in nursing students to Turkish : a validity and reliability study
pmc-12512955.creator: Halil Ibrahim Gules, Gulten Sucu Dag
pmc-12512955.description: BackgroundNurses’ resuscitation self-efficacy levels are a key component in the acquisition of basic resuscitation skills. However, there is no measurement tool to determine nursing students’ resuscitation self-efficacy in our country. This study was conducted to adapt in the nursing students the Basic Resuscitation Skills Self-Efficacy scale to Turkish and determine its validity and reliability.

pmc-12736263.title: Effects of Long-Term Heavy Metal Exposure on Oral Microbial Antibiotic Resistance Genes of Residents in the Mining and Smelting Area
pmc-12736263.creator: Huan Li, Keke Yang, Hongling Liu, Susu Cao, Yuanyuan Bao, Lu Feng, Li Zhang, Jingping Niu, Tian Tian, Hirokazu Kimura
pmc-12736263.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). Growing evidence highlights the role of heavy metals in driving the co-selection of an-tibiotic resistance genes (ARGs), and the human oral cavity is an important reservoir of ARGs. This cross-sectional study investigated the effects of heavy metal exposure on human oral microbiota and ARGs, collecting buccal mucosal and blood samples from residents in a heavy metal-contaminated area (Baiyin City) and a non-contaminated area (Yuzhong County, Lanzhou City).

pmc-13065476.title: Identifying suitable mussel cultivation sites in European offshore waters—an assessment for co-location with the wind industry
pmc-13065476.creator: Enora M Lecordier, Pierre Gernez, Krysia Mazik, Ethan Clark, Rodney M Forster
pmc-13065476.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Ensuring food security is a vital challenge. To meet food and, especially, protein demand in the next few decades, the aquaculture industry needs to expand. This could be achieved by expanding marine aquaculture at sea. Moving aquaculture plots further offshore has gained interest due to its increased space availability and more stable conditions compared to coastal areas, while also mitigating the effects of climate change extremes inshore.

pmc-13256292.title: Intra-Species Response Variability of Listeria monocytogenes and Salmonella enterica to Lemon Essential Oils in Cheese- and Fish-Based Spreadable Foods
pmc-13256292.creator: Raimondo Gaglio, Antonio Alfonzo, Giuliana Garofalo, Rosa Guarcello, Valeria Guarrasi, Nicola Francesca, Giancarlo Moschetti, Luca Settanni
pmc-13256292.description: This study examined the growth dynamics of Salmonella enterica and Listeria monocytogenes in two food matrices, cheddar cheese sauce (CCS) and salmon spreadable paste (SSP), and assessed the antimicrobial efficacy of freshly extracted essential oils (EOs) from Citrus limon cv. Femminello Santa Teresa (FST) compared with commercial (COM) EOs.

pmc-13420718.title: Post-Pneumonectomy Syndrome Causing Reversible Right Ventricular Dilation and Tricuspid Regurgitation
pmc-13420718.creator: Cecilia Villa Etchegoyen, Juan M Farina, Dana M Ellis, Kevin Chen, Reza Arsanjani, Kristen A Sell-Dottin, Staci E Beamer, Samine Ravanbakhsh
pmc-13420718.description: BackgroundPost-pneumonectomy syndrome is a rare complication caused by excessive mediastinal shift and cardiac rotation, leading to nonspecific cardiopulmonary symptoms.Case SummariesWe report the cases of 2 patients who developed cardiopulmonary symptoms after having left pneumonectomy for lung cancer. In both cases, multimodality imaging demonstrated an early mediastinal displacement with cardiac rotation.
